paper_metadata.title: Interstitial carbide synergistically strengthening high-entropy alloy CoCrFeNiV0.5Cx

evidence.quote: A series of high-entropy alloy CoCrFeNiV 0.5Cx (x = 0.01, 0.02 , 0.03 and 0.04) with low C content was fabricated.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure and uniformity of alloy structure before deformation
evidence.quote: In Fig. 1 (a), the XRD spectrum of the as-cast alloy is a single FCC structure, but the diffraction peaks are relatively rough, indicating that the alloy has a poor crystallization and there is a certain component segregation.
after annealing at different temperatures, a large number of M 7C3-type interstitial carbides are produced at temperatures of 700 °C and above.

Each element of the FCC is evenly distributed in the matrix, and the element content is basically the same as the nominal content of the alloy.
the size of the carbide is about 0.5 μm.
The diffraction spots obtained by the FFT in Fig. 8 (c) are also verified as an ordered FCC (L12) structure.

We speculate that this non-stoichiometric carbide generation process first generates VC and then due to the existence of a large number of carbon vacancies, the aggregation of Cr elements is induced by VC to generate an ordered FCC (L12) structure.
In the recrystallization area, there are a large number of fine equiaxed grains, and the size of the equiaxed grains is about 2 μm according to statistical software analysis.
In the non-recrystallized area, there are still large layered deformed grains with severe lattice distortion.

Cold rolling deformation can generate a large number of dislocations in the alloy, and these dislocations easily accumulate at the phase and grain boundaries.
It is this layered alternating structure that allows the alloy to maintain its strength while increasing its shape.

Ordered interstitial carbides (MxCy) with non-stoichiometric carbon vacancy configurations are easy to form in the completely recrystallized region of the alloy after annealing, which is beneficial to the formation of dimples, while maintaining the strength and improving the plasticity of the alloy.
